short: Augustus built a third forum around a temple vowed forty years earlier at Philippi.
full:
Octavian vowed a temple to Mars Ultor, Mars the Avenger, on the eve of the Battle of Philippi in 42 BCE, in revenge for Julius Caesar's assassination. Ground was not broken until after 20 BCE, once the Parthian standards lost by Crassus had been recovered by negotiation, an event the temple came to celebrate alongside vengeance for Caesar. The finished complex, dedicated in 2 BCE, paired the temple with a colonnaded forum lined with statues of Roman generals and of the legendary kings of Alba Longa, tracing an ancestry from Aeneas to Augustus himself.

The forum relieved the overcrowded Forum Romanum and the neighbouring Forum of Caesar, hosting law courts and the ceremonies by which young men took the toga of manhood. Its scale and its genealogical statue gallery set the template for the imperial fora that followed under Trajan, and its high boundary wall, built of the local volcanic stone peperino faced in marble, doubled as a firebreak protecting the forum from the crowded Suburra district behind it.
